beats.role_note: Evidence: the real build-state.json of both first-attempt test reels.
beats.narration_text: My first install, with Claude Code, got further than you'd think. I built two test videos. The narration was generated. Some animations even rendered. But both builds ended the same way: the build-state file says failed, review pipeline, exit two. Neither video made it to a finished cut.

show.event: two folder cards slide in: binary-search-test, claude-liam-ribosomes-read-mrna
each card opens its real build-state.json: status failed, Review pipeline failed (exit 2); 'failed' marked in terracotta
a 'final cut' slot at the right stays empty, outlined dashed

beats.role_note: Evidence: a real frame rendered by the first attempt; the stage row shows where it stopped. Causes per the owner's account (older-Python packages; gates).
beats.narration_text: Two problems sat underneath. Some packages needed an older Python than the one on my machine. And the build kept stopping at its gates: deliberate checks that halt the pipeline when something isn't right. I spent hours patching symptoms. Eventually I deleted the old install and started over.

show.event: a real frame from the first attempt's Manim clip, captioned
'packages wanting an older Python' with accent bar
'gate checks halting the build' with accent bar

beats.role_note: Evidence: the real clone command and the real setup guard message; the folder move that cleared it.
beats.narration_text: Second attempt: a clean copy, and Claude Code again, but this time every error got read before anything was fixed. The setup check stopped at once, claiming a paid voice service. It was a false alarm: videos explaining that check, stored inside the toolkit. Moved out, the check passed.

show.event: terminal line: 'ElevenLabs reference found — this toolkit is Kokoro-only for narration.' with a ✗
inside a 'brutalist/' box, a 'youtube/brutalist/' folder highlights
the folder slides out of the box; the ✗ flips to 'clean' ✓

beats.role_note: Evidence: the real Windows python3 message, the version constraint, the three real commands.
beats.narration_text: Then the first attempt's problem came back. My Python was too new for the animation library, and on Windows the scripts couldn't even find it by name. One fix covered both: a separate Python three point twelve environment, a python three command inside it, then the toolkit's own installer.

show.event: version line 3.10 … 3.14; a shaded 'manim < 0.19 works here' band; marker 3.14 lands outside it
terminal line: 'python3 → Python was not found; … Microsoft Store'
three command lines light in order: py -3.12 -m venv .venv · cp python.exe python3.exe · ./setup --install

beats.narration_text: Then the check that matters. Voice: ready. Captions, animation, scenes, compiling: ready. One row stays blocked: equations need LaTeX. This video has no equations, so that one can wait.

show.event: rows captions, Manim beats, Remotion beats, slates/compile, fonts → ready ✓ in order
tag beside it: 'not needed for this video'

beats.role_note: VERDICT artifact. Portrait: Manim card replaces ClaudeVerdictArtifact916 (fixed-size card failed gate V underfill at 29%).
beats.narration_text: Three lessons. Read the error before fixing anything; the first wall wasn't what it looked like. Gates are checks, not bugs; they stop a build so a broken video doesn't ship. And isolate your Python. Same tool both times. The difference was the approach.

show.event: verdict card in: label 'Verdict', heading 'What I learned'

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — prompt read aloud verbatim and discussed.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's a prompt to try in Claude Code before your next install: "Check whether my machine can run this repo. Test each dependency for real, and before installing anything, explain why each failure happens." The last part matters most: it makes Claude find the cause before it changes anything. That's what made my second install work.

show.event: the prompt types into the composer

props.command: Check whether my machine can run this repo. Test each dependency for real, and before installing anything, explain why each failure happens.
output: look for: each check actually run, not assumed
look for: a cause named for every failure
look for: no installs until you agree
